terms.comment: A description of ours: literally, come too late for the plane, with sērius, Traupman’s “too late” (pp. 87, 337). Traupman and Morgan–Owens have no phrase for missing a plane or a train; Traupman’s miss, dēsīderāre (p. 155), is to feel the lack of someone.

sources: Theodōrus et pater · Ad Larem avītum, Libellī I–VII, as they stood on 7 November 2026, with their glosses. Examples marked “Libellus” quote those texts word for word; classical passages are cited by author.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 87, 155, 337.
